_before_applying: No code, script or receipt in this repository applies this configuration; a repo-wide grep finds no consumer. It is a declaration of intent, so it cannot be assumed to be protecting or deleting anything today.

The 14-day expiry targets segment-fleet-v1/staging/, which is where finalizer.finalize_surface writes before promoting. It calls store.add_artifact_set with staged['staging_uri'] and only then calls artifact_store.promote, so between those two calls the artifact_sets row is the sole reference to an object under an expiring prefix.

The obvious remedy -- promote before registering -- is WRONG, and this was verified against the real PostgreSQL control plane rather than reasoned about: add_artifact_set is also the lease gate. It rejects a stale lease token and transitions the task to UPLOADED. Promoting first would publish an artifact grown under a lease another worker had already taken over, which is a worse failure than the expiry. The current order is correct.

Residual exposure is therefore bounded and was measured, not estimated: a worker interrupted in that window loses one grow attempt, recoverable by retry. No surface row is created because nothing is promoted, so no scientific evidence is lost. tests/test_fleet_postgres_contention.py pins all three properties and passes 3/3 against a real control plane.

If the exposure is still judged unacceptable, the correct remedy is to lengthen this expiry beyond the maximum plausible finalization window, or to exclude staging objects referenced by a non-terminal attempt row. It is not a reordering of the state machine.
